method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, recurrence-invariant and index-range audit, reverse paraphrase and exact formula/macro/token/reference comparison with documented projections. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Recursive coding of rooted optionally labelled trees and a primitive-recursive enumeration of every coded subtree.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A tree is a possibly labelled root node alone or a root joined to immediate subtrees. Its code is a sequence beginning with the number k of immediate subtrees, followed by their codes and then any node label.
samples.checks: The recursive order k,d_1,…,d_k, placement of labels, one-node example and labelled root-with-two-children example are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: SubtreeSeq(t) returns a sequence whose entries are the codes of all subtrees of the tree coded by t, and the function is primitive recursive.
samples.checks: The proposition's object, code level, label and primitive-recursive conclusion are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: ISubtrees extracts positions one through the child count. A corrected fold g starts empty and appends f of entries 0 through k−1, so h obtains immediate subtrees of every entry. hSubtreeSeq accumulates the root and all subtrees through successive levels, possibly with repetitions, and t bounds the depth.
samples.checks: OLCMP-010 states the cumulative through-level invariant implemented by the unchanged hSubtreeSeq recurrence. OLCMP-011 repairs the fold's empty case and off-by-one indices; three QA projections reconstruct the frozen formulas solely for parity comparison.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercise requests an alternative hSubtreeSeq definition in which each subtree code occurs only once.
samples.checks: The source's acknowledgement of repetitions and the uniqueness requirement are both explicit, and the proposition reference options are exact.

source_observations: T041 supplies the established tree and root register, while T314 records the source-defined node, immediate-subtree, leaf and level terms.
MR-P147 directly supports the sequence and subsequence vocabulary used for all tree codes.
No exact official graph-theoretic Marathi headwords for the complete rooted-tree group were exposed by the bounded search; the recursive definitions control the transparent compounds.
OLCMP-010 and OLCMP-011 record the cumulative-level and fold-index repairs.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The exact node, immediate-subtree and leaf compounds remain expert-reviewable.
No TeX reader build was run for this source-only unit checkpoint.
